8 ways parents quietly hurt their kids. Even the most loving parents miss these. 🎒

Jonah is seven, and his mom loves him. But every small hurt is another stone in his backpack:
1️⃣ Always correcting.
2️⃣ Comparing him.
3️⃣ Dismissing his feelings. "Stop crying."
4️⃣ Only noticing what's wrong.
5️⃣ Silence as punishment.
6️⃣ Love that disappears when he messes up.
7️⃣ Never saying sorry.
8️⃣ There, but not there. 📱

In one study, 48% of parents said their phone interrupted time with their kids three or more times a day (McDaniel & Radesky, Child Development, 2018).

By ten, Jonah stops showing her his good grades. 💔

You don't need to be a perfect parent. You need to be one who notices. ❤️ So one night, Mom puts the phone down, kneels beside him, and they take the stones out, one by one.

"Come to me, all who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest." Matthew 11:28 🙏 We can carry every stone to the cross.

At twelve, Jonah doesn't hide. ❤️ Jesus heals what we hurt, and He helps us carry our kids' worries too.
